svg.aria-label: Space-time diagram showing why frames must last at least a round trip of the cable

g.text: Alice hears Dave’s signal while she’s still sending: collision detected ✓
…the collision arrives after she’s stopped listening ✗

ol.li: Time runs down the page and distance runs across. Alice starts a long frame; its front edge takes a while to crawl down the cable (the slope). Just before it reaches Dave, he hears silence and starts sending too. The signals crash near Dave, and Dave’s signal crawls back towards Alice. It reaches her while she’s still sending, so she hears the collision and knows to retry.

Same timing, but Alice’s frame is short. She finishes sending, hears no collision, and moves on, sure it worked. Dave’s signal only reaches her afterwards. Nobody will ever resend this frame: it’s silently lost.

The fix: every frame must last at least as long as a round trip to the far end of the cable and back. That sets a minimum frame size (and, the other way round, a maximum cable length). Short messages get padded with filler to reach the minimum.

figure.figcaption: Why a frame can’t be too short: a sender only notices a collision while it’s still talking.
